claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand the age of the child or children you're claiming for. Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age.

**How old is your child (or what are the ages of your children)?**

Please tell me:
- The name of each child
- Each child's age or date of birth

This will help me guide you through the right checks for your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he would normally qualify for Child Benefit. However, I need to check a few more things to confirm your eligibility. Let me proceed with the next question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 8 years old, he falls into the under 16 category. Now I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in any paid work?**

(This is typically not an issue for an 8-year-old, but I need to confirm for the eligibility assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. Since Alex is not working, let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about any benefits Alex might be receiving:

**Is Alex NOT receiving benefits in his own right?** This would typically mean benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, this is unlikely for an 8-year-old, but I need to confirm for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's only 8.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

For context, this typically wouldn't apply to an 8-year-old, but I need to confirm:
- Is Alex NOT in any apprenticeship, OR
- Is he potentially in an approved apprenticeship (only Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales are approved)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's only 8 and still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. Child Benefit has residency requirements. Let me ask you about this:

**Where do you normally live, and what is your residency status?**

Please tell me if:
1. You normally live in the UK, OR
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
3. You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and if so, what's your situation - working, studying, jobseeking, or have sufficient resources?), OR
4. You're a Crown servant living abroad, OR
5. You live abroad but have another qualifying circumstance

What applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So you normally live in the UK in Manchester. That means you meet the residency requirements. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. The key question is:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and upkeep?**

This means:
1. You live with Alex, OR
2. You contribute to his upkeep (e.g., paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents) at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount, OR
3. You're paying maintenance towards his care under a court order or agreement

What applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone told you they're claiming for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming for him?
- Is another family member claiming?

Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only one claiming for Alex. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. Living at home with you normally, OR
2. In hospital, OR
3. In care (residential or institutional care), OR
4. Fostered with another family?

What's his living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living at home with me normally - nothing special going on.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for his housing and upkeep yourself, without council support? (This is typically the case for most families, but I need to confirm for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I pay for everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards his care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's all the information I need. You've met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me process this and give you your final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **Good News! You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**For: Alex (age 8)**

---

### **Why You're Eligible:**

You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex:
- ✅ He's under 16 years old
- ✅ He's not working full-time (he's in primary school)
- ✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for his care
- ✅ No other person is claiming for him
- ✅ He's living at home with you normally
- ✅ The council isn't paying towards his care

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or **by post using form CH2**

2. **You'll need to provide:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address

3. **Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some of the benefit through tax
   - Even if you think you might be affected, it's still worth claiming as you may not have to repay anything depending on your exact circumstances

4. **Payments:**
   - Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks directly into your bank account
   - If you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits, you can request weekly payments instead

---

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
